claims.limitation: It does not examine primary mathematics learning-gap diagnosis or tuition centres in Singapore.; It focuses on middle school algebra in state schools rather than primary mathematics or tuition centres in Singapore.; However, the study focuses on public school teachers in Indonesia rather than private tutors in Singapore.; This study examines general literacy and numeracy diagnostic approaches in Indonesian public primary schools rather than specifically focusing on primary mathematics tutoring centres in Singapore.; Academic study, abstract-level; not evidence of purchasing by Singapore tuition centres. evidence.title: Leveraging natural language processing for automated assessment and feedback production in virtual education settings
evidence.quote: The average time spent on manual evaluation was 62.2 seconds, while automatic evaluation shortened the time to 36.98 seconds.
evidence.finding: The paper finds that manual evaluation and feedback production take significant time (average 62.2 seconds per instance), supporting the claim that assessment demands substantial effort, though it focuses on general online education rather than primary mathematics diagnosis by tutors in Singapore.
evidence.limitation: It does not examine primary mathematics learning-gap diagnosis or tuition centres in Singapore.

evidence.title: Elementary teachers’ use of adaptive diagnostic assessment to improve mathematics teaching and learning: A case study
evidence.publisher: International Electronic Journal of Mathematics Education
evidence.quote: This case study examined teachers’ perceptions and use of adaptive diagnostic assessment for improving teaching and learning of elementary-level mathematics.
evidence.finding: The study found that elementary teachers perceive adaptive diagnostic assessment as valuable for improving mathematics instruction and efficiency, which supports the notion that educators value tools that streamline diagnostic processes.
evidence.limitation: The study examines public elementary school teachers rather than commercial tuition centres in Singapore.

evidence.title: AI Versus Human Feedback in Mixed Reality Simulations: Comparing LLM and Expert Mentoring in Preservice Teacher Education on Controversial Issues
evidence.publisher: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
evidence.quote: Findings reveal that human experts offered more mixed and nuanced feedback than ChatGPT-4o and Perplexity, especially when identifying missed teaching opportunities and balancing classroom discussions.
evidence.finding: This study showed that human experts offered more nuanced feedback than AI models, bearing on the claim by highlighting the limits of automated tools in delivering the depth of value customers expect.
evidence.limitation: It investigates teacher training via mixed reality simulations rather than commercial math diagnostics for tuition centres.

evidence.title: Following the Impact Chain of the LA Cockpit: An Intervention Study Investigating a Teacher Dashboard's Effect on Student Learning
evidence.quote: The analysis of n = 355 feedback messages sent by teachers through the LA Cockpit revealed that the dashboard assists teachers in identifying students facing difficulties and that teachers mostly provided process feedback, which is known to be effective for student learning.
evidence.finding: The intervention study shows that teachers actively use dashboards to identify students facing learning difficulties, providing partial backing for the utility of diagnosis tools.
evidence.limitation: It examines secondary school classrooms rather than commercial tuition centres.

evidence.title: Can ChatGPT Replace the Teacher in Assessment? A Review of Research on the Use of Large Language Models in Grading and Providing Feedback
evidence.quote: This article presents a systematic review of empirical research on the use of large language models (LLMs) for automated grading of student work and providing feedback.
evidence.finding: This systematic review finds that large language models accelerate the grading process and deliver rapid feedback at scale, supporting the general market demand for assessment tools that save time.
evidence.limitation: It reviews general assessment and feedback research across various subjects rather than specifically examining primary mathematics diagnostic software adoption in tuition centres.

evidence.title: Examining the Process of Middle School Math Teachers Diagnosing and Eliminating Student Misconceptions in Algebra
evidence.quote: The aim of this study is to examine how middle school mathematics teachers diagnose and attempt to eliminate students' misconceptions in algebra.
evidence.finding: The study found that middle school mathematics teachers resort to conventional methods and struggle to thoroughly diagnose student misconceptions in algebra, making the diagnostic process demanding and time-consuming, which supports the claim about the effort required for gap diagnosis.
evidence.limitation: It focuses on middle school algebra in state schools rather than primary mathematics or tuition centres in Singapore.

evidence.title: A Comprehensive Review on Automated Grading Systems in STEM Using AI Techniques
evidence.quote: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of artificial intelligence-powered automated grading systems (AI AGSs) in STEM education, systematically examining their algorithmic foundations, mathematical modeling approaches, and quantitative evaluation methodologies.
evidence.finding: This review highlights that AI-powered automated grading systems enhance grading efficiency, provide instant feedback, and reduce educators' workloads in STEM education.
evidence.limitation: It provides a broad review of mathematical modeling in STEM automated grading rather than empirical evidence of tuition centres spending money on math diagnostic tools.

evidence.title: Preservice Teachers’ Perceptions of AI in Education
evidence.quote: The survey results revealed that a significant majority of participants (88.9%) used generative AI tools for personal learning or teaching preparation, with 92% using text generators like ChatGPT.
evidence.finding: The paper finds that educators show general interest in experimenting with generative AI tools for teaching preparation, which makes one slightly more confident that educators might be open to diagnostic automation tools.
evidence.limitation: It investigates preservice teachers in California higher education rather than commercial tuition centres in Singapore.

evidence.title: Mathematics Teachers’ Interviewing Strategies for Diagnosing Students’ Learning Obstacles
evidence.quote: The purpose of this study is to analyze the interviewing strategies that mathematics teachers use in order to diagnose students’ learning obstacles.
evidence.finding: This study demonstrates that mathematics teachers must employ complex social-emotional and didactical-pedagogical interviewing strategies to diagnose student learning obstacles, which aligns with the claim that diagnosing learning gaps takes substantial effort. However, the study focuses on public school teachers in Indonesia rather than private tutors in Singapore.
evidence.limitation: However, the study focuses on public school teachers in Indonesia rather than private tutors in Singapore.

evidence.title: Mutation-Based Error Diagnosis in a Web Intelligent Tutoring System for First-Degree Equations: A Quasi-Experimental Study
evidence.publisher: Anais do XXXVII Simpósio Brasileiro de Informática na Educação (SBIE 2026)
evidence.quote: This paper investigates the use of mutation analysis as a mechanism for diagnosing student errors in a Web-based Intelligent Tutoring System for first-degree equations.
evidence.finding: The paper investigates a Web-based Intelligent Tutoring System utilizing automated mutation-based error diagnosis for first-degree equations, which bears on the claim by demonstrating automated diagnostic features in math systems, though it lacks tutor review and commercial focus on tuition centres.
evidence.limitation: It does not evaluate human-tutor-reviewed or traceably evidenced reports tailored for tuition centres in Singapore.

evidence.title: Evaluating Trust in AI, Human, and Co-produced Feedback Among Undergraduate Students
evidence.quote: Findings revealed that when the source was blinded, students generally preferred AI and co-produced feedback over human feedback regarding perceived usefulness and objectivity.
evidence.finding: The study demonstrates that students and teachers value the perceived usefulness and objectivity of AI-generated feedback, which supports the premise of value for educational customers, though it evaluates undergraduate contexts rather than commercial tuition.
evidence.limitation: It lacks evidence regarding primary mathematics diagnostic tools and Singaporean tuition center workflows.

evidence.title: Predictive Learning Analytics and University Teachers: Usage and perceptions three years post implementation
evidence.publisher: International Conference on Learning Analytics and Knowledge
evidence.quote: Predictive learning analytics (PLA) dashboards have been used by teachers to identify students at risk of failing their studies and provide proactive support.
evidence.finding: The study demonstrates that university teachers use predictive learning analytics dashboards to identify struggling students, supporting the premise that educators value tools for diagnosing student difficulties.
evidence.limitation: It focuses on distance learning university teachers rather than Singaporean tuition centre operators.

evidence.title: Automated Grading and Feedback Systems: Reducing Teacher Workload and Improving Student Performance
evidence.quote: The results clearly show that grading time was reduced, and it was found to have decreased from 15 hours per week to 9.75 hours per week – a reduction of 35%.
evidence.finding: Results show that automated grading and feedback systems decreased teacher grading time from 15 to 9.75 hours per week, aligning with the premise that educators benefit from and adopt workload-reducing technologies.
evidence.limitation: The research studies general classroom automated grading rather than diagnostic software specifically targeted at primary mathematics learning gaps in tuition centres.

evidence.title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN ARTICULATE STORYLINE-BASED COGNITIVE INTERACTIVE DIAGNOSTIC ASSESSMENT IN VOCATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL MATHEMATICS: A NEEDS ANALYSIS
evidence.publisher: SOSIOEDUKASI : JURNAL ILMIAH ILMU PENDIDIKAN DAN SOSIAL
evidence.quote: The results indicate that conventional assessment practices are not yet sufficient to identify students’ prior knowledge comprehensively.
evidence.finding: The study highlights that conventional assessment practices are insufficient to comprehensively identify prior mathematical knowledge and that teachers require tools with immediate feedback and review features, making the market gap for detailed diagnostic tools plausible.
evidence.limitation: It investigates vocational high school math needs in Indonesia through a needs analysis rather than auditing existing commercial software offerings for tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable reporting in Singapore tuition centres.

evidence.title: The Impact of AI-Generated Instructional Videos on Problem-Based Learning in Science Teacher Education
evidence.quote: This study investigates the impact of AI-generated instructional videos, designed using established instructional design principles, on self-efficacy, task performance, and learning outcomes in science teacher education.
evidence.finding: The study finds that AI-generated instructional tools enhance learning outcomes and task performance, supporting the broader premise that educational technology delivers functional utility to instructors.
evidence.limitation: It examines pre-service science teacher education rather than commercial math diagnostic tools used by private tutors.

evidence.title: Empowering Teachers with AI: Co-Designing a Learning Analytics Tool for Personalized Instruction in the Science Classroom
evidence.publisher: International Conference on Learning Analytics and Knowledge
evidence.quote: The planned sequences were evaluated in a blinded fashion by an expert, and the results demonstrated that the experimental group – teachers who received the clusters with the explanations – designed sequences that addressed the difficulties exhibited by different groups of students better than those designed by teachers who received the clusters without explanations.
evidence.finding: The paper demonstrates that teachers using explainable clustering algorithms designed better instructional sequences to address specific student difficulties, indirectly supporting the premise that diagnostic tools provide value to educators.
evidence.limitation: It evaluates general science teachers in a co-designed research project rather than commercial tuition centres in Singapore using a primary mathematics diagnostic tool.

evidence.title: Identifying Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) Approach Practices in Primary School Learning
evidence.publisher: Urwatul Wutsqo: Jurnal Studi Kependidikan dan Keislaman
evidence.quote: The results indicate that TaRL is implemented through three key stages: initial diagnostic assessment to map student ability levels, grouping based on literacy and numeracy levels, and level-based differentiated instruction accompanied by ongoing formative evaluation.
evidence.finding: The study identifies initial diagnostic assessment as a key stage of the TaRL approach in primary learning and notes that it creates increased teacher workload and time constraints, which supports the claim that diagnosing learning gaps takes substantial effort.
evidence.limitation: This study examines general literacy and numeracy diagnostic approaches in Indonesian public primary schools rather than specifically focusing on primary mathematics tutoring centres in Singapore.

evidence.title: K-12 Teachers’ Acceptance and Resistance Perceptions of Learning Analytics Adoption: A Mixed-Methods Approach
evidence.quote: How do teachers describe their motivation and readiness for LA adoption?” The findings indicated that the factors facilitating LA adoption were performance expectancy, social influence, and feelings.
evidence.finding: The study identifies key performance expectancy and social influence factors driving K-12 teacher adoption of learning analytics, lending indirect support to the idea that educators see value in automated diagnostic insights.
evidence.limitation: It looks at general K-12 school adoption rather than commercial tuition centres in Singapore.

evidence.title: Multi-Agent Architecture for Formative Assessment: An Integrated Approach to Error Diagnosis and Diagnostic Feedback
evidence.publisher: International Conference on Computer Supported Education
evidence.quote: We present a multi-agent cognitive architecture for automated formative assessment that operates using a sub-2B parameter language model (Qwen3-1.7B), allowing low resources and local execution.
evidence.finding: The paper presents a multi-agent AI architecture for automated error diagnosis and formative assessment in grade-school mathematics, supporting the feasibility of diagnostic tools, but it evaluates automated generation rather than tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable reports specifically deployed in tuition centres.
evidence.limitation: It does not evaluate commercial market offerings or human-tutor-reviewed reports in tuition centres in Singapore.

evidence.title: A review of the impact of formative assessment on student achievement in mathematics
evidence.publisher: NOMAD Nordic Studies in Mathematics Education 22(3)
evidence.quote: The results show positive relations between student achievement in mathematics and the ways of doing formative assessment.
evidence.finding: Formative assessment is positively related to maths achievement, which supports the value of diagnosis but not that centres would pay for a tool.
evidence.limitation: Academic study, abstract-level; not evidence of purchasing by Singapore tuition centres. Gap: Does not address primary-level diagnosis tools or purchasing by tuition centres.

evidence.title: The effect of a formative assessment practice on student achievement in mathematics
evidence.quote: The 14 teachers who participated in the PDP taught a total of 291 students (the intervention group). The students belonging to this group were 148 females and 143 males. The remaining 15 teachers (6 females, 9 males) that taught year-7 mathematics that school year taught a total of 275 students (the control group).
evidence.finding: The study evaluated mathematics achievement outcomes for 291 intervention students and 275 control students across participating secondary schools.
evidence.limitation: The study measures general secondary mathematics achievement rather than specifically diagnosing primary mathematics learning gaps.
